name: Motion Illusions
description: Why movement can appear to reverse, continue, or arise from a still pattern.
intro: Motion perception combines changing image information, attention, and assumptions about the world. These demonstrations reveal how a moving—or entirely stationary—image can make the visual system infer movement.

name: Ambiguous Perception
description: One image, multiple ways to see it.
intro: Some pictures allow two stable interpretations. Our perception may alternate even when the stimulus does not change, revealing that seeing involves active interpretation.

name: Color & Brightness
description: Color is influenced by the light and shapes around it.
intro: Color and brightness are not measured in isolation by our visual system. Context and adaptation can make identical values appear surprisingly different.

name: Geometry & Size
description: How context alters judgments of length, shape, and size.
intro: Our brains interpret geometry using contextual cues. Equal segments may appear unequal, and straight lines may appear slanted.

name: Depth & Perspective
description: How a flat image becomes a convincing sense of space.
intro: We infer three-dimensional structure from shading, perspective, motion, and prior experience. When cues conflict, perception may be strikingly wrong.

name: Attention & Awareness
description: What we notice, overlook, and see fade away.
intro: Vision is selective. Attention, eye movements, and neural adaptation change which parts of the world reach awareness.
